speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me how long you have been experiencing chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort, and if there have been any changes in your bowel habits like urgency or blood in the stool.

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS-D) with functional diarrhea, likely triggered by a prior Campylobacter or similar bacterial infection (post-infectious IBS). The symptoms of cramping relieved by defecation, urgency, mucus, and incomplete evacuation are classic for IBS. The camping history suggests a possible infectious trigger, but the chronic nature and symptom pattern strongly point to a functional disorder. No further tests are needed at this stage unless red flags develop. Please ensure you maintain good hydration and dietary fiber intake. If symptoms worsen or new symptoms like weight loss or fever occur, seek immediate care.
